plan.angle: Plague Report in Russia: Quarantine Lifted. What's Confirmed? (as of Oct 8). Lines, each credited to its source: Rospotrebnadzor (Oct 8): nearly 5,000 lab tests found no dangerous pathogens, medical monitoring was completed for over 90% of contacts, quarantine measures were lifted, and it called reports of a second case 'fake'. WHO: it does not know what caused the Oct 2 death and has asked Russia for more information. WHO's initial risk assessment (reported Oct 6): moderate to low in Irkutsk oblast, low for Russia, very low for the WHO European Region. Teaching line: not confirmed isn't ruled out. Plague hasn't been officially confirmed. Close with 'If you're worried, talk to a health professional.' About 60–70 s.

plan.why: The biggest status change since the death (radar momentum 93, peak in 0–3 days). The update angle is new, since the 10-07 decoder predates the lifted quarantine, and question-decoder titles are our proven format. | fact-check: A good dated decoder, but tighten three lines to match what was actually reported. (1) Rospotrebnadzor (Oct 8) reported medical monitoring completed for 'over 90%' of contacts, not 'contact observation has ended'. (2) The test figure was 'nearly 5,000'. (3) Rospotrebnadzor called the second-case reports 'fake' (AP/PBS, Oct 8); present that only as its denial. WHO's 'moderate to low / low / very low' rating is described as an initial risk assessment (reported Oct 6). PBS/AP reported that WHO had not issued a formal assessment, so call it 'WHO's initial risk assessment' and date it. WHO (Van Kerkhove, ~Oct 7–8) says it doesn't know what caused the Oct 2 death and has asked Russia for clarification. Re-check at publish time.

factcheck.summary:
I checked every factual claim against its source and all of them hold up. The dates, numbers and credits are correct:
- The death was on Oct 2 (AP).
- On Oct 8, Rospotrebnadzor reported nearly 5,000 lab tests with no dangerous pathogens, monitoring completed for more than 90% of contacts as of Oct 7, and anti-epidemic measures completed (IRK.ru). It also denied a second case (AP, Vedomosti).
- AP published on Oct 8 and reports that WHO's Van Kerkhove spoke "on Wednesday". That was Oct 7, 2026, so scene 6's date is correct. She said WHO doesn't know the cause of death and urged Russia to share more information.
- WHO's Oct 6 risk tiers come from Lindmeier's briefing, and the script quotes them exactly.
- The pneumonic warning signs match CDC's list, and the WHO fact sheet (29 Sep 2026) exists.

Status framing is correct throughout: the case is called "suspected", plague is "not officially confirmed", and the script says not confirmed isn't ruled out. The safety and urgent-care lines are present, and the script avoids fear-bait and stigma.

What's left is wording polish:
- The quote marks around 'fake' are on a paraphrase.
- The hook "measures are over" could read as an all-clear.
- Rospotrebnadzor's own "no plague case registered" statement is left out. Including it would give balance.
- The CDC source is missing its last-reviewed date.
- The script is about 188 words, a little over the 170-word guide. That's still well within the 178 s limit.

audio.soundNotes: Music is already well-centered (-13.5 dB under voice, -13.9 in pauses) so left at 1.0×; no change needed there. Thinned the SFX kit heavily: dropped ~20 near-duplicate simultaneous layers (e.g. swoosh+whoosh, tick+bubble pairs) that were stacking 4–7 effects into under a second around the contacts-stat and chips-reveal moments, keeping one clear anchor sound per beat per the transition type. Nudged the ding on "Nearly 5,000," the swell on "Moderate to low," and the swell on "Not confirmed ≠ ruled out" up slightly since those are the three key reveals/payoffs and were sitting a touch under the -14 to -20 dB speech window; pulled one over-loud pop at 62s back down. Added four subtle custom cues (document stamp, notification ping, reassurance chime, soft exhale swell) to mark the Rospotrebnadzor statement, the WHO risk label, the "moderate to low" reassurance, and the bottom-line close — all calm and non-alarmist, in keeping with the channel's measured tone on this topic.
